newsitem.title: USA: Microtest lowers Q1 view, revises '96 data.
newsitem.headline: Microtest lowers Q1 view, revises '96 data.

text.p: Microtest Inc said it had revised downward its results for the 1996 full year and fourth quarter, and would fall short of internal operating expectations for the 1997 first quarter.

Richard Meise, Microtest chairman and chief executive officer, said, "During 1997, we are making changes in the structure of the end user direct sales program, and the changes will impact operating results for the first quarter of 1997."
He said Microtest had also been affected by "an overall slowing" in the growth of the network products industry, and this would also hurt first quarter operating results.
"Accordingly, we will not meet internal operating expectations for the quarter," Meise said in a company statement released Thursday.

Microtest, a developer of local area network products, said its final audited results for the 1996 fourth quarter showed net revenue of $12.2 million and a net loss of $15.1 million, or $1.86 per share. Previously, it reported net revenue of $14.3 million and a net loss of $14.1 million, or $1.73 per share.

Excluding a purchased research and development write-off and non-recurring expenses related to the acquisition of Logicraft Information Systems Inc, fourth quarter net income was $0.6 million, or $0.07 per share, compared to previously announced net income of $1.6 million, or $0.19 per share.

For the full year 1996, net revenue was $50.4 million, with a net loss of $11.6 million, or $1.43 per share. Previously it reported net revenue of $52.5 million, with a net loss of $10.7 million, or $1.31 per share.

Excluding the Logicraft R&D write off and non-recurring expenses related to the acquisition, net income was $4.1 million, or $0.50 per share, compared to previously announced net income of $5.0 million, or $0.61 per share.

Richard Douglas, Microtest chief financial officer, said the revision in the results was due to "a recent determination by the company that reserves relating to end user direct sales were inadequate."

"In the results, gross revenues recognized with respect to end user direct sales remain unchanged, but net revenues attributable to such sales decreased as a result of an increase in the reserves for fourth quarter sales made through OMI's direct sales program," he said.
